provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Enormous tickets and long sales cycles; many prospects already have an agency, so openers target gaps (no timeline, no feasibility, dated galleries). Not a beginner category. No pool equipment brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Design to first swim: the pool construction timeline
pageStructurePlus.contains: Design and rendering, permits, layout and dig, steel, shotcrete, plumbing and electrical, tile and coping, decking, interior finish, fill and start-up, with what the owner does at each stage
pageStructurePlus.why: A pool takes months and the yard is a construction site. Buyers choose the builder who shows them the whole road.

pageStructurePlus.section: Will a pool fit? Backyard feasibility
pageStructurePlus.contains: Setbacks, easements, septic and utility lines, slopes and retaining walls, excavator access through the side yard, HOA approval and soil surprises
pageStructurePlus.why: Many buyers aren't sure their yard qualifies. A feasibility page turns that doubt into a booked site visit.

pageStructurePlus.section: The whole project budget, not just the pool
pageStructurePlus.contains: Shell, decking, safety fence, lighting, heater, automation, landscaping repair, permits and the first season of chemicals, laid out as ranges per item
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers get burned when the pool price grows by the end. Showing the full project wins trust early in a long cycle.

pageStructurePlus.section: Safety barriers and swimming pool code
pageStructurePlus.contains: Barrier fence heights, self-closing gates, door alarms, safety covers, drain safety and what the inspector checks before you can swim
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents decide on safety first. A clear code page shows the builder handles inspection and protects kids.

pageStructurePlus.section: Spas, water features and pool equipment choices
pageStructurePlus.contains: Attached spas, sun shelves, sheer descents, fire bowls, variable-speed pumps, heaters, salt versus chlorine and phone-controlled automation
pageStructurePlus.why: Features drive the ticket and the excitement. A features page helps buyers build the pool in their head before the design meeting.

designDirections.name: Backyard Consult
designDirections.bestFor: Smaller pool builders and fiberglass installers who win on a fast backyard consultation
designDirections.whyItFits: Cobalt on white reads like clean water, and the grotesque type keeps the consult button and timeline crisp.

designDirections.name: Built to Swim
designDirections.bestFor: Custom pool builders with years of finished backyards, from bare dirt to first swim
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom pools built from dig to first swim in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Warm linen lets the water be the only blue on the page, and brick red sits naturally with coping stone and pavers.

designDirections.name: Evening Water
designDirections.bestFor: Luxury builders selling vanishing edges, spas and full backyard resorts
designDirections.headlineSample: Luxury swimming pools designed for {City} estates
designDirections.whyItFits: A midnight ground with champagne accents shows lit water at dusk, and Didone headings match a six-figure buying decision.

openers.line: For a company building inground pools, it's rare to see no site on the listing. A family about to spend that much on a pool will study every finished backyard before calling.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a pool buyer would find behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your link goes to Facebook, where your best pool builds are mixed with dig-day posts and holiday greetings. Buyers on a long research cycle need a portfolio they can return to.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note the most impressive finished pool there.
openers.linkLine: Your pools, organised for buyers who research for months: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site has nice pool pictures but nothing on how a build actually goes, from dig to first swim. That's the question every buyer asks in the first meeting.
openers.hook: Check their site for a construction timeline or process page. If missing, use this.

openers.line: On a phone your pool gallery loads slowly and the consult form won't submit. Pool research happens on phones in the evening, over months.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your pool site, fast on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask {Business Name} whether a pool fits a yard without calling. Buyers would send a lot survey, yard pictures and a rough budget first.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a form that takes a survey or pictures. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A backyard feasibility request for pool buyers: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reels from dig day to the first cannonball are the story every pool buyer wants. They're scattered across a year of posts.
openers.hook: Find a build they documented in stages. Mention it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your pool builds, stage by stage on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about a crew that kept them informed through a long build and a pool finished in time for summer. That's what a nervous buyer needs to read, and it's stuck on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about communication or timing. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the pools they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Families who want to swim by summer sign pool contracts in winter. The builders who are easy to research in December fill their dig calendar first.
openers.hook: Use from October to February. Mention their usual build lead time if they post it.

openers.line: Pool decisions get made by couples at the kitchen table at ten at night. A consult request and budget guide that works then keeps them from moving on to the next builder.
openers.hook: Call after hours. A generic or full voicemail means the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A pool consult request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring for your pool construction crew. Skilled finishers and tile setters look at the quality of a builder's pools before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note role and date.
openers.linkLine: A pool builder site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You build pools across several towns around {City}, but nothing tells a family in {Neighborhood} you've built there. Seeing a pool down the road is what convinces them.
openers.hook: Find towns in their posts or reviews; use the most affluent one they name.
openers.linkLine: A pool page for each town you build in: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you work with pool lenders, say so on the budget page. For many families the monthly number is the real pool decision.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing anywhere public. Otherwise skip.
openers.linkLine: Pool financing explained before the consult: {demo-link}

openers.line: A swimming pool means permits, inspections and a licensed contractor. Showing your licence, insurance and how you handle every inspection settles a buyer's biggest fear.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry for a record. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and inspections on one pool page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every pool you build hosts a summer of parties, and the guests ask who built it. They still look you up before calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning friends or neighbours. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next pool referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you finished is a stunning pool. A build like that should be the first thing a family sees when they look you up.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished pool and name its features: shape, spa, sun shelf, town if tagged.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} is a beautiful pool.

I was looking at pool builders in {City} and found {Business Name}, but nothing online walks a family through your build from dig to first swim or lets them ask whether a pool fits their yard. I built a sample pool site to show the idea, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like to see it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample pool builder site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a dig-to-swim timeline, a backyard feasibility request, and a whole-project budget page. If it's not a fit, say so and I'll step back.
sequence.call:
"Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for pool builders in {City}. I sent a note about a sample site for {Business Name}. Did you get a chance to look?"

IF NO:
"No problem. It's a sample with your pools organised by build, a dig-to-swim timeline, a feasibility request for buyers unsure their yard fits, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What stood out?"
 → listen, then ask how long their average buyer researches before signing
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many build stories and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and updates. For a builder your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, a small fraction of one pool."
"Fifteen minutes this week to go through it?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before winter design season."

objections.handler: "Keep them for ads. The sample shows the pages buyers ask for that most pool sites skip: the build timeline, feasibility and the full project budget. I can build just those."
"Then the site's job is better buyers, not more. A feasibility form and budget page filter out the families who can't fit or afford a pool before your designer's evening is gone."

objections.objection: Pool buyers come from referrals and the home show.
objections.handler: "They do, and they research for months afterwards. A site that answers their questions keeps you in the running until they sign."

objections.objection: We don't want to publish prices.
objections.handler: "The budget page shows ranges per item, not a quote. It protects you from the buyer who thinks the shell price is the whole project."

objections.objection: I've been burned by web people before.
objections.handler: "Fair. You've seen the sample before paying anything, the scope fits on one page, and the domain stays in your name."
"{Build Range}. For you, around {Build Price}: build stories, a timeline, a feasibility request, a budget page and town pages."

email.subject: Pool builder site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for pool builders in {City} and made a sample for {Business Name} with a dig-to-swim timeline. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm archiving the {Business Name} pool demo on Friday.

Shall I keep it up a little longer? One word is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, families who want to swim next summer are starting to research builders now. Thought of {Business Name}.

The sample pool site is still up, same price: {demo-link}

bullets: Price by build story, not page: each finished pool told from dig to first swim is the unit that sells.
The feasibility request with survey and picture upload is the most valuable piece; price it on its own line.
Expect agency comparisons. Quote the pages agencies skip as add-ons when the builder already has a site.
Peg the build to the cost of a single pool feature, like a spa or a fire bowl, never to hours.
Budget extra review rounds; pool owners are careful and the sales cycle is long.
Add the safety and code page to every build; it answers the parent's first question.

lineItems.description: Max with stage-by-stage pictures from dig to first swim, a feature list and a short video.
Max with survey upload, yard pictures, access notes, HOA status, budget band and routing to the designer.
Max with stage illustrations, owner to-dos at each stage and local permit notes.
Max with ranges per feature, a printable checklist and financing notes.
Max when each page shows pools built in that town and local permit notes.
Max for a narrated tour of two or three finished pools with captions.

whatElseYouSell.name: First-swim day photo and drone shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Shoot the pool the day the family first swims, from the drone and at dusk with the lights on. That's the shot every future buyer remembers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on the next pool start-up.

whatElseYouSell.name: Build-stage documentation for a whole season
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "I document one swimming pool from dig to first swim on a few visits. It becomes the build story buyers read for months."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, on a build the owners agree to share.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for pool builds
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a pool at some stage of the build goes on your Maps profile with the town, so the listing shows real work all year."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after the first swim
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A week after start-up, when the kids have been in the pool every day, the family gets a note asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Winter pool planning campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A winter campaign for 'swim by summer' backyard consultations reaches families while they're planning, not when every builder is booked."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in September, run November through February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Home show booth and printed lookbook
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A booth graphic and a printed lookbook of your pools, with a feasibility request code, turns home show traffic into site visits."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, ahead of the next home show.

whatElseYouSell.name: Past-client pool party referral event
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A past client hosts a summer evening at their pool, and prospects booked through the site meet the builder and the family."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 8, in summer, with a willing past client.

withoutAI.route: Pool fence and safety barrier installers
withoutAI.whoPays: The fence company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every pool you build needs a barrier that passes inspection. The fence crew you use needs a site, and they'll send pool leads back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Required by code on every job; the trades already work together.

withoutAI.route: Pool service companies that take over after start-up
withoutAI.whoPays: The pool service company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "After start-up, someone cleans the pool weekly. The service company you recommend needs a booking site, and they hear about remodels first."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Service techs see every aging pool; builders hand off every new one.

withoutAI.whoPays: The hardscape builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The hardscaper who builds the kitchen next to your pool has the same high-ticket buyer. Introduce me and both sites link."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same family, same season, bigger joint projects.

withoutAI.route: Pool lenders and home improvement loan officers
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The loan officer who finances your pools needs a page that explains pool loans plainly, with builders they work with."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Lenders have marketing budgets and the pool builder is their best referral source.

withoutAI.whoPays: The lighting company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your pools look best lit at night. The lighting installer who does that needs a site full of your pools at dusk."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Lighting makes the pool builder's photos better; the referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "New pool owners walk into the supply store confused about chemicals. A site with a water testing booking page and new-owner guide helps them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Stores want new-owner loyalty and the builder sends every new owner there.

withAI.route: Barrier code checker for the fence installer
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners describe their yard and pool and the assistant lists what the local barrier code needs, then books the fence quote."
withAI.whyItWorks: Code questions slow sales; your pool client's knowledge trains it.

withAI.route: Water chemistry assistant for the supply store
withAI.pitchLine: "New pool owners type their test strip readings and get plain advice from the store's own guidance, plus what to buy."
withAI.whyItWorks: It brings new owners back to the store weekly.

withAI.route: Loan pre-check helper for the lender
withAI.pitchLine: "Pool buyers answer a few questions and see the monthly payment range for a pool project before they apply."
withAI.whyItWorks: Lenders get warmer applicants, and pool builders close faster.

withAI.route: Service route intake for the pool service company
withAI.pitchLine: "New pool owners from the builder are asked pool size, equipment and gate access, and slotted onto the weekly cleaning route."
withAI.whyItWorks: Every new pool becomes a service customer with no phone tag.

withAI.route: Joint backyard enquiry assistant for the hardscaper
withAI.pitchLine: "The hardscaper loses the kitchen sale when it's quoted months after the pool. A shared intake catches the outdoor kitchen wish while the family is still designing the pool."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells bigger joint projects, and the hardscaper sees it working for a partner.

withAI.route: Dusk preview for the lighting installer
withAI.pitchLine: "Pool owners upload a daytime picture and get a clearly labelled night preview with lights in the water and the landscape."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells lighting on new pools and sends credit to the pool builder.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for pool enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Missed calls from pool shoppers get a text asking their town, when they hope to swim and whether they have a lot survey handy."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for finished pools
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families write long, happy reviews after a pool build. You get a draft thank-you that picks up their details, and you edit it on your phone in a minute."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Pool project budget builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Buyers pick pool size, spa, decking, fence and features and see a whole-project range, so the first design meeting starts from a real number."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price bands by size and per feature.

softwareAI.name: Milestone draw invoicing for pool builds
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit, then draws at dig, shotcrete, tile and start-up, each invoiced automatically when the stage is marked done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their draw schedule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Feasibility brief from survey and yard pictures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the uploaded survey and yard pictures it drafts a one-page brief: setbacks, likely pool footprint, access and red flags for the designer to verify."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past feasibility notes and local setback rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Owner build-progress portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families see each pool construction stage with pictures, inspection dates and what they need to choose next, instead of calling the office."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stage list and a project manager posting updates.

softwareAI.name: Stage-change texts to homeowners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the pool moves from dig to steel to shotcrete, the family gets a text with what happens next and how long it takes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the progress portal live.

softwareAI.name: After-hours pool consult assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening calls, asks about the yard, timing and budget band, and books a backyard consultation with your designer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar and qualifying questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Selections tracker for tile, coping and finish
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each family's tile, coping, interior finish and equipment picks are tracked against allowances and deadlines, so the crew never waits on a choice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their selection list and allowance rules.

softwareAI.name: Pool design concept from a backyard picture
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A family uploads their backyard and sees two clearly labelled pool concepts placed in it, to react to before the design meeting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their pool shapes and a set of finished backyards. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Permit and inspection tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every pool's permit, steel inspection, barrier check and final are tracked by town, so no crew shows up before the inspector signs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their towns' inspection steps.

softwareAI.name: Swimming pool chatbot on timelines, code and features
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'how long does a gunite pool take' and 'do I need a fence' from your own guidance, and books a consult when they're ready."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their timeline, code notes and feature list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew schedule across concurrent builds
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Dig, steel, shotcrete, tile and plaster crews scheduled across every active pool, with subs notified when a stage slips."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their crews, subs and typical stage durations.

softwareAI.name: Design meeting notes to proposal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Record the design meeting and it drafts the pool proposal: size, features, allowances and exclusions, for the designer to finalise."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their proposal template and pricing. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Warranty and first-year check-in sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New pool owners get check-ins at one month, the first winter and one year, with warranty reminders and an offer for upgrades like a heater or cover."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs warranty terms and the upgrade list.

softwareAI.name: Build story writer for portfolio pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From stage pictures and project notes, it drafts the dig-to-swim story for each finished pool, which you approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs portal updates and sign-off. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by stage and sub
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See margin per pool by stage once excavation, steel, gunite, tile, plaster and equipment invoices are in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs a season of sub invoices and change orders.

softwareAI.name: Change order approvals on the phone
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the family adds a sun shelf or upgrades the tile mid-build, the change is priced, signed on their phone and added to the next draw."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their change pricing and the draw invoicing in place.

softwareAI.name: Remodel and resurfacing lead scorer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners of older pools upload pictures of the plaster and tile, and it scores whether it's a resurface, a remodel or a repair before the visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, for builders who also remodel. Needs labelled past remodel pictures. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sub onboarding checklist and site rules app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New tile setters and plaster subs sign off your pool site rules and safety steps on their phone before their first day, so the super stops repeating them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs their site rules and onboarding checklist.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Pool project budget builder sold to other builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every pool builder loses evenings to families who thought a pool cost far less than it does. The budget builder fixes that for a monthly fee."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: High-value buyers per seat, and the first client paid for the logic.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer locator for a pool equipment manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pool equipment or fiberglass shell manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Families who like your shells or equipment need an authorised builder nearby. A locator with build stories sends them to your dealers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer programs, and the pool client shows you know the builder side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Pool and spa association member toolkit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members get a dig-to-swim timeline, barrier code page and feasibility request they can add to their own sites."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want members to look professional and safe.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency licence for pool timeline and feasibility pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Most pool builders already have an agency. License them the timeline, feasibility and budget pages their sites are missing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Sells to the agencies that already own these clients.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each dealer in your network gets a local page with your shell models, their installs and a feasibility request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want dealers selling more shells and lack local pages.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every pool builder you finance gets a co-branded payment calculator and application page on their site."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Lenders pay to be built into the buying path.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Luxury home builder resort backyard packages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Buyers of custom homes want the pool designed with the house. A backyard package page in your design studio sends it to one pool builder."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders want upgrade revenue and a reliable partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Community and HOA pool renovation bid portal
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Community pools need resurfacing and code updates. A bid portal with specs and pictures makes it easy to compare pool contractors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers run these projects rarely and need structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Builders signing contracts in winter for spring digs need to know where steel, gunite and equipment are heading. A note built from invoices they contribute."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Long lead times make cost trends matter; shared data keeps it honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Hotel and resort pool refurbishment showcase
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A refurbished resort pool needs a booking page that shows it off, and your client built it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Commercial owners have bigger budgets and the pool builder has the relationship.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One custom pool builder per metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A pool builder in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I take one pool builder per metro so the timeline, feasibility and budget pages stay unique to you. Your metro is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity matters at this ticket size.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Replace agency pool sites that stalled
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pool builder unhappy with an agency
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your agency site looks fine but never explains your build, I can rebuild it around the pages pool buyers actually read."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Frustrated builders already budget for a site; they want one that works.

upsellLadder.offer: Pool builder site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The pool site and the care plan go on one contract, so each finished pool's build story goes up with one message."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after first swim and Google profile posts
upsellLadder.trigger: The first pool started up since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That family just had their first swim. Let's ask for the review while the kids are still in the water."

upsellLadder.offer: First-swim day photo and drone shoot
upsellLadder.trigger: A pool start-up is scheduled, or the gallery still uses placeholders.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot the next pool on first-swim day and at dusk. It'll lead your portfolio for a year."

upsellLadder.trigger: Feasibility requests show buyers with budgets far below a real pool project.
upsellLadder.line: "Too many consults end at the first number. The budget builder shows families the whole pool project before they book."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention the office fielding 'what's happening with my pool' calls.
upsellLadder.line: "Those status calls are what the portal ends. Families see every pool stage with pictures."

upsellLadder.offer: Feasibility brief from survey and yard pictures
upsellLadder.trigger: Feasibility requests outpace the designer's time to review them.
upsellLadder.line: "Your designer can't review every survey before the visit. A one-page pool brief on each saves hours a week."

upsellLadder.trigger: A stage slips and idles a sub, or they take on more concurrent builds.
upsellLadder.line: "That idle plaster crew was a scheduling miss. One schedule across every pool build stops it."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first anniversary of pools built since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "Last year's pools are a year old. A check-in with a heater or cover offer is the easiest second sale to a pool owner."
